w: This evening, after the balaks and kishores performed a drama, Swamishri blessed the assembly, saying, " When a person indulges in worldly attractions he gets destroyed. Bad influences can affect him at any age. No matter how intelligent a person may be but when he goes to a gambler he cannot resist playing a bet. This is simply because of the influence of an immoral atmosphere. Don't the boys and girls revel together in discos! But that does not give happiness, while this (Satsang) is the immortal nectar that gives ever-lasting happiness. "We look upto T.V. T.V. The problem is we have not exercised discrimination from the beginning and that is why we feel like watching it..."

The Yogi Jayanti celebration was held beneath the newly inaugurated mandir dome. In his blessings Swamishri said, "Yogiji Maharaj's virtues and glory were extraordinary. His saintliness and love can never be forgotten. Mulshankar Vyas of Zambia has never forgotten the laughter of Yogiji Maharaj which he had experienced only once. Those who have received his pat (dhabbo) never forget it … Such was his divine state."

Divya Sannidhi Parva - Bal Karyakar From 20 May to 22 May, a special 2-day camp for volunteers (karyakars) of the children's wing commenced at 6:40 pm in the presence of Swamishri. More than 450 male and female karyakars had arrived for this divine treat. To energise, guide and appreciate the Karyakars' tremendous effort in inspiring children with values, education and satsang, the camp comprised of interactive programs, skits, dramas, speeches and question answer sessions with senior sadhus, and blessings from Swamishri. The karyakars were further inspired to effectively organise their efforts through time and resource management, human relationships, etc.
From 20 to 23 May Swamishri blessed the Bal Pravrutti Divya Sannidhi Parva.

Since the inception of the BAPS Children’s Forum (Bal Mandal) by Yogiji Maharaj in 1954, today, through the inspiration of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, it has grown to 3,020 bal mandals and 2,200 balika mandals in India and abroad (total of 5,220 bal mandals). It has a membership of 100,000 children from standard 1 to 8. More then 75 sadhus and 7,500 male and female volunteers are actively running the bal-balika mandals.

The main theme of the shibir was ‘Atmabuddhi’. On the inaugural day a drama ‘Eva Santne Namu Hu Shish’ was presented by the volunteers. Swamishri addressed the volunteers in this respect, “Today, you have arrived for the shibir. You have come to consolidate your personal glory for God and His Sadhu, faith in them, atmabuddhi in them and to become brahmarup and make this your last birth. Gunatitanand Swami has said, ‘We have got this birth to become akshar-rup and worship Purushottam.’ This birth will be worthwhile only when we offer devotion to God, listen to discourses of His glory and do satsang… to become free of material desires and bhakti to God. Yogiji Maharaj established the bal, kishore, yuvak and mahila mandals. Without the Gunatit Sadhu it is not possible to become brahmarup because one is engrossed in worldly pleasures.” During the three-day programme Swamishri and the senior sadhus addressed 100 sadhus and 650 male and female volunteers, there were question-answer and interactive sessions with Swamishri, dramas and a celebration of Swamishri’s 55th Pramukh Varni Din on 21 May.

At 10.20 am Swamishri took off from Kampala and landed at Dar-es-Salaam International Airport, in Tanzania at 12 noon. Swamishri was welcomed with garlands by Subhashbhai Patel (Chairman of Tanzania Satsang mandal), Minister for Cultural Sports and Media, and Deputy Minister of Labour Work and Acquirement Mr. Mummad S. Khatif and Immanuel Cheembi respectively. Thereafter Swamishri arrived at the BAPS mandir amidst jubilant ‘jais’ from devotees and children showering flower petals. Shri Kantibhai Patel, a senior devotee, and Subhashbhai Patel garlanded and honoured Swamishri. Then Swamishri took lunch and retired for the afternoon.

In the evening Swamishri arrived for the welcome assembly at the Lakshminarayan Mandir. Bhaktavatsal Swami gave the welcome address on behalf of all and then the youths of Dar-es-Salaam performed a traditional welcome dance. Thereafter Mahendrabhai Barrister, Subhashbhai Patel and Ashwinbhai Sampat (Chairman of Sanatan Mandir) gave welcome speeches. Then heads of various religious organizations and mandirs welcomed Swamishri and the sadhus with garlands. In conclusion Swamishri blessed the assembly, “We can attain everything in life, but our shastras say that if fail to attain devotion to God, dharma, satsang and other virtues then our life is worthless. God has given us this human body and intelligence. Animals cannot understand right and wrong whereas man can think because God has endowed him with extra powers. Therefore a person should always think about the purpose of life. Human birth is attained out of punya acquired through pilgrimage, yoga, yagna, charity and other means. May we all through this priceless human birth do such works that it gives peace to one’s soul…”

ds.t: A seed became a banyan tree
w: After puja, Swamishri came to his residence and met all the devotees sitting in the meeting room. Among them was the headman of a village. About a month and a half earlier he had given up alcohol at Swamishri's hands, and since then his bravery had turned to the path of devotion. He had vowed to help 51 brave young men like himself give up alcohol, and even now some who had given it up were with him. Swamishri was pleased and said, "Just keep going like this. The whole village will be happy and addictions will go. My blessings are that bad company and disunity leave the village."
